Pakistan recently flight-tested its first indigenously developed air-to-air missile (AAM), named Fa’az (Urdu for victorious). This development marks a significant step for the country, which has so far relied primarily on Chinese- and US-made missiles. For India, this development merits attention, as recent standoffs between the two countries have been characterised by aerial engagements and Pakistan could potentially use the missile in a future conflict. Watch ThePrint's Bantirani Patro explain Pakistan's AAMs and potential implications for India.
